hero.title: Funeral Receptions
hero.lede: After a funeral, people need somewhere quiet to sit down together. We can arrange a private room, tea and coffee, and a buffet or a warm meal, often at short notice, and you don't need to decide everything at once.

sections.title: A funeral reception at Bentley Hotel
sections.html:
A funeral reception, or a purvey as many people in Lanarkshire still call it, is the part of the day when the formality is over and the family and friends who have gathered can sit down, talk and remember. It doesn’t need to be elaborate. It needs a warm room, something to eat and drink, and people who will look after the practical things so that the family doesn’t have to.

That is what we offer. For a smaller gathering we lay the conservatory beside the restaurant; for a larger one, our function suite seats up to 100. We serve tea and coffee as people arrive, and then either a buffet or a warm sit-down meal from our own kitchen, whichever suits. The bar is there for anyone who would like a drink. We’ll take care of the room so that you can give your attention to the people who have come.

Arrangements can be made in a single phone call, by a member of the family or by whoever is helping with the funeral, and we can usually do so at short notice. Numbers at a reception are hard to predict and often change on the day; we understand that, and we plan for it. Nor do you need to settle everything at once: tell us the date and a rough number, and the rest can be decided in the days that follow.

Parking at the hotel is free and Motherwell station is about 5 minutes’ walk; by road, we are close to junction 6 of the M74. For relatives travelling from further away, the hotel has 18 en-suite rooms.

sections.title: The room, the food and somewhere to stay

items.title: A room of your own
items.text: The conservatory for a smaller gathering, or the function suite for up to 100 seated. Quiet, private and set aside for you for the afternoon.

items.title: Tea, coffee and a meal
items.text: Tea and coffee as people arrive, then a buffet or a warm sit-down meal from our own kitchen, with a bar for anyone who would like a drink. We agree the food with you in plain terms.

items.title: Rooms for family
items.text: For relatives travelling from further away, we have 18 en-suite rooms in the hotel, with a full Scottish breakfast cooked to order when it is part of the rate. Parking is free and the station is about 5 minutes' walk.

sections.title: Funeral receptions: what people ask us

items.q: How quickly can you arrange a reception?
items.a: Often within a few days, if the room is free. Call us on 01698 265588 with the date and a rough number and we’ll tell you straight away what we can do. Whoever is helping with the funeral is welcome to call on your behalf.

items.q: We don't know how many will come. Does that matter?
items.a: No. Numbers at a funeral reception are always uncertain, and we plan for that. Give us your best estimate when you book and a firmer number the day before if you can, and we’ll do our best to allow for a few more.

items.q: Do we have to choose the food now?
items.a: No. Tell us the date and roughly how many to expect. The choice between a buffet and a sit-down meal, and what is on it, can wait a day or two, and we’ll go through this season’s options with you simply, by phone or in person.

items.q: Can we have the room to ourselves?
items.a: Yes. The function suite is a private room, and for smaller gatherings we set the conservatory aside for you.
